title: Best Privacy Browser Extensions & Ad Blockers Compared
metaDescription: uBlock Origin, Ghostery, Privacy Badger and DuckDuckGo's add-on compared with Incognito Browser (which we make) on blocking, ease of use and customization.
intro: Protect your online privacy with the right browser extensions. This page compares four privacy add-ons, and one Android browser with an ad blocker built in, on the same four criteria: ad blocking, tracker blocking, ease of use and customization.

products.name: uBlock Origin
products.tagline: Open-source ad and tracker blocker with fine-grained filter controls
pros: Blocks ads and trackers effectively, with regularly updated filter lists
Advanced filtering options and custom rule creation
Open source with transparent development
Full version runs in Firefox, including Firefox for Android
cons: Interface can be overwhelming for beginners
May break some websites without proper configuration
Chrome no longer runs the full version and Edge is phasing it out by the end of 2026; uBlock Origin Lite is the more limited replacement

products.name: Privacy Badger
products.tagline: EFF's tracker blocker that stops third parties seen tracking people across sites
pros: Blocks trackers without filter lists to manage
Developed by EFF with strong privacy credentials
Minimal false positives on legitimate websites
Simple interface with little to configure
cons: Blocks only ads that track you, not other ads
Relies on EFF's regularly updated tracker list; learning from your own browsing is off by default

products.name: Ghostery
products.tagline: Tracker and ad blocker that shows which trackers each site loads
pros: Shows detailed information about blocked trackers
Clean, user-friendly interface
Anti-tracking and ad blocking in one extension
Smart blocking that rarely breaks websites
cons: Fewer advanced filter controls than uBlock Origin
Drew data-collection criticism under a previous owner, which sold it in 2017

products.name: DuckDuckGo Search & Tracker Protection
products.tagline: Simple privacy protection from the privacy search engine
pros: Blocks trackers and forces HTTPS connections
Sends Global Privacy Control and blocks tracking cookies
Works without setup
Integrates well with DuckDuckGo search
cons: Blocks ad trackers, not ads themselves

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser with an ad blocker built in, instead of an add-on
pros: Built-in ad blocker, with a High Security Blocking option
Runs in private mode all the time; history, cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit
Settings to turn images, JavaScript and cookies on or off
No add-ons to install or keep updated
cons: A separate browser, not an extension for the browser you already use
Android only: no iOS, desktop or web version
Tracker blocking and custom filter rules are not among its listed features
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics

features.name: Ad Blocking
features.description: Blocks display ads, pop-ups, and video ads

ublock-origin.note: Blocks ads with regularly updated, customizable filter lists

privacy-badger.note: Blocks ads that track you, but not other ads: it is a tracker blocker, not an ad blocker

ghostery.note: Blocks ads with filter lists, including on YouTube and Facebook (per Ghostery)

duckduckgo-privacy-essentials.note: Not an ad blocker: it blocks ad trackers, not ads themselves

incognito-browser.note: Built-in ad blocker, with a High Security Blocking option since May 2026

features.name: Tracker Blocking
features.description: Prevents websites from tracking your browsing behavior

ublock-origin.note: Comprehensive tracker blocking with regular updates

privacy-badger.note: Blocks trackers that ignore its opt-out signals, using a tracker list EFF keeps updated

ghostery.note: Blocks trackers from its tracker database

duckduckgo-privacy-essentials.note: Blocks third-party trackers and tracking cookies

incognito-browser.note: A tracker blocker is not among its listed features; cookies can be switched off and are wiped when you exit

ublock-origin.note: Works out of the box; advanced features need setup

privacy-badger.note: Install and forget; works from a tracker list EFF keeps updated

ghostery.note: Ad blocking, anti-tracking and Never-Consent are on from install, with no setup needed

incognito-browser.note: No add-on to set up; private mode is always on

features.name: Customization
features.description: Ability to customize blocking rules and settings

ghostery.note: Good options for trackers and ads, with fewer filter controls than uBlock Origin

incognito-browser.note: Switches for images, JavaScript, cookies and High Security Blocking; custom rules and per-site allowlists aren't listed

verdict.summary: Ghostery and uBlock Origin tie for the top score on these four criteria (Ghostery is listed first alphabetically). Ghostery blocks ads and trackers with nothing to set up, and all of its blocking is free. uBlock Origin offers the most customization, but its full version now runs mainly in Firefox: Chrome no longer runs it, and Edge is phasing it out by the end of 2026. Privacy Badger comes third: it blocks trackers and the ads that track you, but not other ads, so pair it with an ad blocker. DuckDuckGo's extension and Incognito Browser, which we make, tie for the lowest score (DuckDuckGo's is listed first alphabetically). DuckDuckGo's extension is simple, but it blocks trackers rather than ads and has few settings. Incognito Browser is an Android browser with a built-in ad blocker, not an extension, and it doesn't list tracker blocking or custom filter rules.

pro_tips: Always review extension permissions before installing - avoid extensions that request access to all websites unless absolutely necessary
Use uBlock Origin in medium mode for better privacy protection, but be prepared to manually allow blocked resources on broken sites
Combine Privacy Badger with an ad blocker like uBlock Origin for comprehensive protection without conflicts
Regularly audit your installed extensions and remove ones you don't actively use to reduce your attack surface
Test websites in incognito mode first if they break with privacy extensions - this helps identify if extensions are causing issues

faqs.question: Do I need multiple privacy extensions or just one?
faqs.answer: One well-configured extension like uBlock Origin is often better than multiple extensions. However, combining uBlock Origin with Privacy Badger can provide complementary protection without conflicts. Avoid running multiple ad blockers simultaneously as they can interfere with each other.

faqs.question: Why do some websites break when I use privacy extensions?
faqs.answer: Privacy extensions block tracking scripts and ads that some websites rely on for functionality or revenue detection. Most extensions allow you to whitelist specific sites or temporarily disable blocking. Look for the extension icon in your browser toolbar to adjust settings for specific sites.

faqs.question: Are free privacy extensions as good as paid ones?
faqs.answer: Yes. All four extensions compared here are free. Ghostery's optional Contributor plans add extras such as themes and statistics, not extra blocking, and Privacy Badger is made by the EFF, a donor-funded non-profit. Paying doesn't by itself make an extension block more: check who makes it, what it blocks and what permissions it asks for.

faqs.question: How do I know if a privacy extension is safe to install?
faqs.answer: Check the developer's reputation, read recent reviews, verify the extension is open source when possible, and review the permissions it requests. Avoid extensions that ask for excessive permissions or have poor reviews mentioning suspicious behavior.

faqs.question: Can privacy extensions slow down my browsing?
faqs.answer: They can. Blocking ads and trackers leaves a page fewer scripts to load, but every extension adds some work for the browser, and several blockers running at once can slow it down and interfere with each other. This page doesn't score speed or memory use, because we have no independent measurements to cite. One well-maintained blocker is usually enough.
